source.quote: Taking on a little bit of water it seems. More than that though, we have some gold farms. And while I do know a couple of gold farms in Wetlands, to be completely honest, I haven't farmed in this zone specifically in a quite a while. So, Goldy's exploration here is going to take quite a bit of research, loot table scouring, and feet on the ground to find out some more farms. But, I did say I knew a couple. And the first thing that comes to mind for me is Wetlands whelp farming. That's right. Much like the bronze whelp of Blasted Lands and dark whelps in Burning Steppes, we have a few more whelps here. Two actually. There is the OG Tiny Crimson Whelpling, a classic battle pet, one that could drop in Wetlands way back in the day from the flame snorting whelps around here. If you watched the last Double Down Burning Crusade video I did, this was the last battle front for Double Down to try to make his double.

source.quote: So, we won't be upset if we snag a few of these pieces. And oh, we snagged quite a few. The drop rate seems to actually be pretty decent on these and we'll target the rest of the set as well, but that's from other mobs in the zone. Starting off, I think I'm liking the Ebon whelp farm. And speaking of which, after not much farming, boom, the Dark Whelp Ring. Again, and pretty lucky for one of our first drops because we got this looted before kill 300, not even an hour of farming. And with it being a one in 1,000 drop rate, I would say a little bit on the lucky side. Very good. Now, one thing I usually do whenever we go into a new zone on Goldbound is check and see if the borders are clean or if there's a new zone bordering our current zone that might accidentally be explored. You know, after the Westfall to Duskwood border incident. So, hopping on to Path of Exile here, my main who can freely cross any borders, I found a couple potentially troublesome spots.

source.quote: Once we get to Kalimdor, any accidental explorations there are going to be the forfeit zone of Deepholm. Again, just off the coast of Kalimdor. The rationale here is that these are two zones that won't come up on the regular zone spins, like the other Cataclysm zones of Highjal and Twilight Highlands. There is just no paths leading straight into the water, so we'll have to get them eventually, and I think this is the best way to have them as a possibility. If I accidentally discover a locked zone, it's relegation to a forfeit zone for 1 week, or until a new wow token is earned, whichever comes first. Pretty much exactly what we did with Darkmoon Faire. Let's hope it doesn't happen here in Wetlands, though, because I'm having a lot of fun discovering some of these farms. Take the cave beside the dangerous Twilight Highlands potential unlock, for example. Luckily, the cave itself in the mountain is unlocked and coded as Wetlands through and through, because there are some things that are definitely worth farming in this cave.

source.quote: First and foremost, there's a rare spawn, the Razormaw Matriarch. And this rare spawn has quite a few decent transmog drops, and two very solid transmog drops, like the Jurassic wristguards. Market values on these bracers float anywhere between 40,000 and 100,000 gold with average sale price being 5,000 gold. So, a good drop for sure. Then, there's also the Beaded Raptor Collar, another solid transmog piece with a value of 10 to 80k, but a bit lower on the average sale price around 1,000 gold. Still a good one to tag. But, we aren't just here for the rare because she also guards a nest. And as far as I know, the nest does have an independent spawn from the rare, but it can contain an egg, the Razormaw Hatchling, which is actually just a pet, one that can be sold for upwards of 1,000 gold. So, yeah, we'll most definitely pop into this cave every now and then and try our luck at the rare spawn and the egg spawn. And if you're counting, which we are, that is three high-value battle pets from the Wetlands so far, and we aren't even done with the battle pets here just yet. Now, the rest of the cave here does have some raptors, and since we currently have skinning, we can check and see what they drop. There isn't anything crazy on their loot tables, but we can snag a few more medium and light leather from these guys.

source.quote: Oh, well, I guess we can always get blue world drops, no matter what the drop tables say. We just pulled the Raptor's Edge, a blue world drop BOE. Maybe a higher drop rate from raptors, I don't know, but it does have a market value of 6,000 to 17,000 gold. A very nice drop from here. Not exactly something we can specifically target for again, but a good one to get while testing. And into the bags and onto the auction house it goes. So far, we've spent most of our time here in the Wetlands on the east, but there's also a few things over in the west that are worth checking out. Over at Welgar's Retreat and Welgar's Excavation Site, we have a few things going on because there's some rock elementals, Paleolithic elementals, plus some living fossils.

source.quote: This farm actually raises a pretty good point because archaeology is actually a skill and a secondary profession in World of Warcraft, but we haven't had a chance to use it yet. The reason? Well, there's just no archaeology trainers in our currently unlocked zones. They're only in major cities in Eastern Kingdoms, which we don't have access to those trainers yet. But, Wetlands opens up an archaeology trainer on the roll over in Kalimdor in Dustwallow Marsh. There's an archaeology trainer there. So, if we do roll that zone, this whole thing, as far as archaeology, may now be on the table. And while archaeology might not be a crazy gold farm, we'll have to wait to see. Once we get archaeology training, we will definitely test it out to see if we can make some coin or at the very least get some upgrades for Goldie from it. Anyways, back to the numbers. How was the gold per hour from farming the elementals?

source.quote: Well, after an hour of farming, we managed to pull in 171 iron ore, not bad, 167 tin ore, 31 cores of earths, and 34 elemental earths. And we actually snaked up 11 essence of earths, which I didn't see on the drop tables, but those are only one gold each anyways. All in all, the trade good value here came out to 1,322 gold per hour. Not amazing, and during this farming hour, we didn't pull in the crimson whelpling either. All this talk with the whelpling though, I think we better get back to a farm that is going to pull in one eventually. One that I can imagine many of you are waiting for me to do, the classic Wetlands hyper spawn farm. So, down to the east of Greenwarden's Grove in the green belt, kind of right in the middle of the spawn location of the even whelps, we have two warring mobs, the even slave hunters and the Dragonmaw Whelp Stealers. And if we stand right in the middle here, where the two forces are clashing, as long as we respect for AoE, we can kill five of the mobs that are fighting, and within 10 seconds or less, five new mobs rush up to take their place. Oh, yeah. This is a no moving, highly AFK-able hyper spawn farm. And there's a few things to farm here.

source.quote: First, of course, and kind of the reason we're here, is the tiny crimson whelpling. It's just a zone drop, and this is probably the easiest spot in the zone to get thousands of kills without too much trouble. So, staying here for a few hours is going to dramatically increase our zone-wide kill count and slowly work towards that one in 10,000 drop. But, on top of that, the slave hunters are dragonkin. They can be skinned. Yeah. And during the hyper spawn, between killing and looting, we pretty much have an infinite skinning farm. They just keep spawning, we keep killing and skinning. Now, they only give light leather and medium leather, which are still one in five gold each respectively, but with how many we should be able to kill per hour, it might end up being a very good consistent trade good farm, too. Plus, every kill here rolls the dice on the tiny crimson whelpling. But, that whelp isn't all that's on these guys' loot tables. They also have a few more pieces of the smoldering set, the chest and the legs.

source.quote: There's a few assorted Dragonmaw here. The ones we want to farm though are the Centurions. Although to get these guys to spawn reliably, we kind of just kill every Dragonmaw on site here. But the Centurions in particular can drop the Dragonmaw Shortsword. This transmog weapon comes in with a ticket price of about 40,000 gold. But postings are pretty sparse on it. And average sales are pretty low. So I don't know what a realistic sale price would be. Likely two to 4,000 gold. But while we're roaming around looking for Centurions, there's also a rare spawn here to keep an eye out for. Garneg Charrskull. Plus his drop of the Ringing Helm. Another 40K transmog piece that could likely fetch some good coin on the auction house. Ironically though, while farming here for a while, neither of these are the drops that I got. I guess maybe Wetlands has a high drop rate of world drop blues because boom.

source.quote: The Darksteel Bastard Sword. A blue two-handed sword BOE zone drop. And I mean, look at this thing. This is a sword I would definitely want to have in battle. And it's also a sword that I want to have on the auction house. With a market value of 150,000 gold. Yep. You heard that right. My hearing stealth blade 2.0. Although I doubt a sale would hit market value on this. It's a pretty high ticket. But I would definitely expect at least 20 to 50,000 gold for this bad boy. And so far Wetlands is delivering. Well, maybe it's all the saved up luck from Molten Core because run 33 and still no Nightslayer Chest and no second binding. Either way though, we only just got into Wetlands this week. But we've already snagged up a few valuable solid battle pets, two world BOE blues, tons of skins, and even some consistent ore farms. So let's go ahead and check the mailbox clear to see how much movement we we have.
